title: Common-fibre coranks of two finite presentations
statement: Let E be a totally disconnected normed field, X any scheme, P a module over its condensed E coefficient ring, C a pro-etale cover, and f_i:R_i^{m_i} to R_i^{n_i} finite free presentations of the inverse images of P. At v in C_i and w in C_j with the same image in X, n_i minus the rank of the continuous presentation matrix evaluated at v equals n_j minus its rank evaluated at w. No noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Example 3.1; agent rank/descent argument in original node, Common-fibre coranks of two finite presentations

proof.text: Form the tensor product of the residue fields of v and w over their common base residue field. It is nonzero because tensoring vector spaces over a field is faithful. Choose a prime and an algebraic closure of its residue field. The resulting geometric point factors through both v and w.

Pull back both presentations to that geometric field. The inverse-image composition comparison and canonical coefficient comparison identify the two resulting modules. Pullback preserves finite biproducts and cokernels.

Evaluate at the final object. Covers of the algebraically closed field split, so evaluation preserves the cokernels. It sends coefficients to E and the presentation maps to the pointwise matrices, by the adjoint test characterization of the continuous realization.
The two matrices have isomorphic finite-dimensional E-vector space cokernels. Rank-nullity gives the displayed equality, including zero rows or columns.
